description:
Reproduce the six reported failures and distinguish regressions from already shipped behavior.

Current state: extend existing Agent Plan functionality; see each task for the verified starting point. This phase follows the baseline discovery and owns only the outcomes below.

Outcomes:
- Produce an evidence-backed baseline for the six user problems and their shared domain contracts.
- Identify existing implementations to extend, including completed F016/F018/F020/F021/F023/F024.

Tasks and boundaries:
- A1: Reproduce the reliability failures on isolated fixtures. A reproducible, bounded baseline identifying the failing layer for each of the six reported problems without changing real project plans.
- A2: Define one shared next-work and context contract. Shared domain inputs, outputs and acceptance cases for scheduling, return precedence, context validity and explicit uncertainty.

Preserve canonical planner identity, phase-scoped handoffs, derived status and session ownership. Read existing code precedents before implementation; use the current task checklist for steps. Source locations are navigation evidence at c4d0c459f74f5365c9ab8a9fe53ad6d7907a8231, not permanent anchors.

Acceptance: All six reports have a reproducible scenario or an explicit evidence gap. Fixtures never write to another real project or its planner. Existing atomic claims and explicit recovery remain covered. There is one explainable precedence rule with zero-priority and tie cases. No current-phase preference silently overrides a higher global priority. The contract does not change the existing warning-only no-task guard.

Design detail: .planner/docs/agent-brain-plan.md. Product requirements: BR01, BR02, BR03, BR04, BR05, BR06, BR16.

Full technical contracts and worked cases are in .planner/docs/agent-brain-registration-handoff.md. Preserve them in execution context; counts/titles alone do not satisfy this phase. Associated task descriptions include their detailed discussion contracts.

Extend the common baseline contracts to independent plan/workspace/runtime identity, task executions, target integration and revision-aware artifact availability. M/N/O then supply these foundations before B scheduling; the six original reliability failures remain required.
Additional outcome coverage: . Full architecture, examples and boundaries: .planner/docs/agent-brain-shared-planner-and-execution.md. The older mergeable .planner policy in inspected source docs is the baseline being evolved; no product migration has run.

Cross-cutting consistency and bounded-cost acceptance (21 October 2026):
Every create/update/move or relationship change checks affected task/phase/feature/project scope and dependency readiness through P128(F025)/T496. Update genuinely obsolete facts only; reviewed-unchanged assessments name exact revisions, and pending semantic obligations remain explicit and resumable. Return indexed affected deltas rather than full ancestor/plan/graph reloads; measure per-flow context/payload/tool budgets without dropping mandatory rules or inventing context retention. BR28 and BR29 apply to this phase. Full contract: .planner/docs/agent-brain-impact-reconciliation-and-token-budgets.md.

tasks.title: Define one shared next-work and context contract
tasks.description:
Outcome: Shared domain inputs, outputs and acceptance cases for scheduling, return precedence, context validity and explicit uncertainty.

Existing state: Selection, recap, lifecycle messages and skill instructions still have separate logic and conflicting read-order guidance. A historical session timestamp is not proof that model context survived compaction.

Implementation responsibility:
- Specify active owned work, actionable pending returns, then globally ready feature → phase → task precedence.
- Define readiness against dependency, parked-state, ownership and explicit-user-selection rules.
- Specify context delivery versus attestation versus conformity evidence; preserve typed non-success results.
- Define shared result shapes used by MCP, Pi, server and UI and map every baseline scenario to an owner.

Acceptance and evidence:
- There is one explainable precedence rule with zero-priority and tie cases.
- No current-phase preference silently overrides a higher global priority.
- The contract does not change the existing warning-only no-task guard.
